verdict.rationale: Terraform's `terraform plan` creates an execution plan that previews changes before apply. `apply` prompts for approval of that plan. Plans can be saved with `-out` and applied exactly as reviewed, inspected via `terraform show` (human-readable or JSON), and include destroy (`-destroy`) and replace (`-replace`) operations. A long-time user independently corroborates its 'meaningful diffs'. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation that plan output itemizes each create, update, and destroy action per resource.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can preview exactly what will change — creates, updates, and destroys — before applying

citations.quote: The `terraform plan` command creates an execution plan, which lets you preview the changes that Terraform plans to make to your infrastructure.
Terraform automatically creates a new execution plan as if you had run terraform plan, prompts you to approve that plan, and performs the indicated operations.
You can use the optional `-out=FILE` option to save the generated plan to a file on disk, which you can later execute by passing the file to `terraform apply`
Use the command to inspect a plan to ensure that the planned operations are expected
These include `-destroy`, which creates a plan to destroy all remote objects
developers can use speculative plans to verify the effect of their changes before submitting them for code review.
